messages:
erin: Heads-up — ran into an odd UX edge when saving per-route saved queries. When a user selects multiple models + route filters, the save modal currently defaults to org-scope and that surprises people when they expect route-scoped views.
sam: Oof. Is that the modal where the 'Apply to all routes with same model' checkbox is checked by default?
erin: yeah, it's checked by default right now. We think the modal should preserve the current context (route) when invoked from a route page.
kevin: leaning that way too. Most folks understand 'Save this view' as 'save current route + filters'. We should still surface the scope prominently in the modal so it's obvious.
erin: proposal: default scope = route when initiated from a route context; default org-scope only from global console. Also add a lightweight preview in the modal: "This saved view will apply to Route: <name> and Models: [list] — estimated traffic & cost impact."
sam: preview sounds good. Does the backend already provide a compact preview API for saved views? @product-bot any constraints (rate limits, auth)?
product-bot: /api/saved_views/preview supports POST with {route, models, filters} and returns sampleMatchCount, top-3-representative-queries, and estimatedTokenRate. Rate limit: 20rpm per user; requires the same auth scope as create_saved_view.
kevin: perfect. UI suggestion: show "Sample matches: 1.2k requests/day", "Estimated token delta: +0.6k tokens/day", and a small badge if any model in the set is traffic < 10%.
erin: also propose 'model weighting' heuristics for the preview so the default included models are traffic-weighted. e.g. pseudo: 
```
suggested_models = models.filter(m => trafficShare(m) > 0.1)
if suggested_models.empty then suggested_models = [models.argmax(trafficShare)]
```
sam: makes sense. For an initial pass I'll wire the preview call and show the counts + sample queries. I'll add a small CTA: "Include low-traffic models" if the preview omitted them.
kevin: backend note: keep an explicit `scope` field in the savedview schema ("route" | "org" | "model") — no silent server defaults. UI can pick a default when calling create.
erin: agreed — explicit scope in API is non-negotiable. Also add an audit flag so admins can see where org vs route views were created.
sam: I'll prototype the modal copy + calls tomorrow and post a screenshot. @kevin can you review the schema change and small preview endpoint contract?
kevin: will review. Tiny ask: preview endpoint should return a deterministic sample (seeded) so the modal preview doesn't jitter for users.
erin: good call. thanks team :thumbsup:
